correctness.rationale: The exact two-count Poisson Fisher determinant is derived from independent count means. A strict monotone Gaussian rearrangement proves the optimal geometry among all measurable sets. The explicitly differentiated derivative numerator has exactly one zero because its second derivative changes sign once, its endpoint derivatives are positive, and its midpoint value is negative. Uniform interpolation-error bounds establish the small-field expansion; tight rescaling yields the large-field limit. The extracted standalone standard-library checker supplies 24,844 deterministic diagnostics, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The present result cannot claim the classical 1.5852 constant, the Fisher identity, the threshold rearrangement principle, or full-pixel estimation bounds as novel. The surviving claim is the exact constrained all-measurable-partition two-channel optimum and finite-field uniqueness, which does not follow from choosing the best radius of a single on-source SNR aperture or keeping full individual pixel counts.

evidence: The two-parameter Poisson Fisher determinant with source/background gradients equals the square of two-bin contrast divided by independent Poisson means. Vicuña et al. explicitly use per-pixel Poisson Fisher sums instead of partitioning all pixels into exactly two totals.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A joint Fisher design need not optimize a fixed binary spatial quantizer: pixel-resolved observations contain higher-dimensional count data, and moving the fitting radius discards or includes pixels rather than moving a boundary separating two retained totals. Our geometry is equivalently a two-valued threshold of the Gaussian likelihood ratio under a fixed area budget; this equivalence is included in the strict layer-cake proof rather than claimed as a new principle.

originality.rationale: Full relevant text in Vicuña et al. (2023), full Masci Gaussian aperture note (2008) and full Chandra background-aperture documentation were compared against the exact two-aggregate-count fixed-field statement. The known large-field Gaussian radius and Fisher/rearrangement tools are credited as prior. No inspected published source establishes the finite-field globally unique two-region arbitrary-measurable partition and its two-parameter Fisher determinant; general quantization prior art and some inaccessible texts remain priority risks, not independent certification.
residual_risks: Classical Gaussian radius 1.5852 sigma is already known and is not an originality claim.
The original Fischer–Kochanski 1993 complete text and Espinosa 2025 full manuscript were not verified fully read; no NOT_COVERING certification is asserted for inaccessible material.
General binary quantization and optimal experimental design literature may imply this special Poisson partition result without matching astronomical terminology.
Local Fisher information is at vanishing source flux; estimator performance at the nonnegative parameter boundary is not established.

value.rationale: A fixed two-channel photon-readout budget gives a concrete information-design problem for joint flux and nuisance sky estimation: one count cannot identify both unknowns. The theorem globally classifies all measurable masks at every finite field radius, disproves equal-area default optimality and quantifies a meaningful information-determinant gain at c=2. The large-field 1.5852 sigma constant is classical; the contribution is the exact finite-field two-parameter all-masks result. A full-resolution instrument remains better and is not contradicted.
